title: Canonical open pro-etale pullback evaluation and its unit
statement:
Let $X,U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, with constant ring sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_U$ on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Use the actual module inverse and direct images $j^*,j_*$ and unit $\eta_j$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with the canonical coefficient identification of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Let $M$ be any sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

There are isomorphisms
$$\rho_{M,W}:(j^*M)(W\to U)\xrightarrow{\sim}M(W\to U\to X)$$
for every pro-etale object $W\to U$, natural in $M$ and in $W$, and linear under the constant-coefficient restriction identification in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Under these isomorphisms, the component of the specified adjunction unit at every pro-etale $V\to X$ is exactly restriction:
$$\rho_{M,V\times_XU}\circ\eta_{j,M}(V)=\operatorname{res}_{V\times_XU/V}:M(V)\longrightarrow M(V\times_XU).$$
Here the codomain of $\eta_{j,M}(V)$ is $(j_*j^*M)(V)=(j^*M)(V\times_XU)$ by the direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and the fibre product is that of [def-pc-fibre-product]. The isomorphisms refer to the actual inverse image constructed on compatible small skeletons as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. No quasi-compactness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion, via localization of the open site; canonical inverse-image evaluation and unit normalization made explicit from the construction in def-weil-proetale-inverse-image.

proof.text: Put $u(V)=V\times_XU$ and let $v(W)$ denote $W\to U\to X$. The localization lemma makes $v(W)$ an ambient site object and identifies restriction of sheaves and coefficient rings. First work in the concrete bounded-object categories. For $W\to U$, let $e_W:W\to u(v(W))$ have projections $\mathrm{id}_W$ and $W\to U$. The first projection is its inverse: the other composite has the same two projections as the identity, since $j$ is a monomorphism. In the category $\mathcal I_W$ defining the actual pullback, $t_W=(v(W),e_W)$ is initial. Indeed, for $(V,\phi:W\to u(V))$ put $a=\mathrm{pr}_V\phi:v(W)\to V$. The equality $u(a)e_W=\phi$ holds on both fibre-product projections. Conversely this equality forces $a=\mathrm{pr}_V\phi$. Thus the required arrow exists uniquely; this uses the actual indexing category, not a different inverse-image functor.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u and its preceding definition of the indexing category; Tag 00XZ, section-localize; specialized using proetale.tex Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion

proof.text: Write $P F(W)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal I_W^{\mathrm{op}}}F(V)$, with coprojections $\iota_{V,\phi}$. The maps $F(a):F(V)\to F(v(W))$ form a cocone: for an indexing arrow $b:V\to V'$, the corresponding maps from $v(W)$ satisfy $a'=ba$, and $F(a')=F(a)F(b)$. They therefore define $q_{F,W}:PF(W)\to F(v(W))$. Its inverse is $\iota_{t_W}$. One composite is the identity because the arrow $t_W\to t_W$ is the identity. The other composite is the identity after every coprojection, since the colimit relation for the unique arrow $t_W\to(V,\phi)$ says $\iota_{t_W}F(a)=\iota_{V,\phi}$. This proves the isomorphism by the colimit universal property, for sets, abelian groups and rings alike; all maps used are morphisms in the indicated category.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u, and remark-functoriality-presheaves-values; explicit initial-index calculation

proof.text: For $b:W'\to W$, restriction sends $\iota_{V,\phi}$ to $\iota_{V,\phi b}$. Since $a_{\phi b}=a_\phi v(b)$, the formula in step 2 gives $q_{F,W'}PF(b)=F(v(b))q_{F,W}$. Naturality in $F$ follows from $h_{v(W)}F(a)=F'(a)h_V$ for every sheaf map $h:F\to F'$. Thus $q$ is a natural presheaf isomorphism $PF\cong F\circ v$. Its target is a sheaf by the localization lemma. The sheafification universal property extends $q$ uniquely to $\theta_F:j^{-1}F=(PF)^\#\to F\circ v$. Explicitly its inverse is the composite $F\circ v\xrightarrow{q^{-1}}PF\to(PF)^\#$. The first inverse law follows from $qq^{-1}=1$; the second follows after precomposition with $PF\to(PF)^\#$ from $q^{-1}q=1$, and hence follows by sheafification uniqueness. The same uniqueness gives both naturality laws for $\theta$.

These calculations apply to the specified small models. For $W$ in the chosen source model, choose a representative $V_0$ of $v(W)$ in the ambient model, with isomorphism $h:V_0\to v(W)$. Replace $t_W$ by $(V_0,u(h)^{-1}e_W)$, including the chosen base-change comparison isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of the model equivalences identifies arrows from this object with arrows from $t_W$, so they remain unique. The cocone map of step 2 is now $F(V)\xrightarrow{F(ah)}F(V_0)\xrightarrow{F(h)^{-1}}F(v(W))$. If a second representative $h':V'_0\to v(W)$ is chosen, the unique comparison is $h^{-1}h'$, and functoriality cancels $F(h^{-1}h')$ in this formula. Consequently the resulting maps are independent of representatives and commute with restrictions, model unit/counit isomorphisms, and coprojections. Step 3 then extends these very same maps uniquely through sheafification. Hence $\theta$ identifies the actual small-model inverse image, with its adjunction, rather than merely some isomorphic left adjoint.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u: explicit coprojections and counit, evaluated on the compatible small skeletons of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], for commutative $\Lambda$ the coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] are identified with the constant sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_U$ by the unique constant-section-preserving isomorphisms, under which the canonical map of the constant-exactness theorem is the structure map $c^j_\Lambda$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; we work with the latter. Write $B=v^*\Lambda_X$ for literal restriction and let $d:\Lambda_U\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be the unique constant-section-preserving ring isomorphism of the localization lemma. Let $c:j^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ be the specified coefficient map. We check $dc=\theta_{\Lambda_X}$. In the Kan adjunction the counit on a generator indexed by $(V,\phi)$ is restriction along $\phi$; thus under $\theta_{j_*G,W}$ it is $G(e_W):G(u(v(W)))\to G(W)$. The definition $c=\varepsilon\circ j^{-1}(\rho^j_\Lambda)$ consequently identifies $c_W\theta_{\Lambda_X,W}^{-1}$ with $G(e_W)\rho^j_{\Lambda,v(W)}$, where $G=\Lambda_U$. This ring map $B\to\Lambda_U$ sends every constant section $a$ to $a$, by the defining property of $\rho^j_\Lambda$. Its composite with $d$ is the identity by uniqueness of extension from the constant presheaf through sheafification. Since $d$ is invertible, this map equals $d^{-1}$. This proves the claimed coefficient compatibility with the canonical $c$, whose invertibility is also recorded in the constant-exactness theorem.

source.place: Tags 00VE (lemma-adjoints-u: counit on coprojections), 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), 00XZ (section-localize); sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules)

proof.text: Apply $\theta$ to the underlying abelian sheaf of $M$. It respects the module action under $\theta_{\Lambda_X}$: on the colimit cocones the equality is $\operatorname{res}(rm)=\operatorname{res}(r)\operatorname{res}(m)$, and after sheafification it follows by uniqueness. Equivalently, naturality of the set-sheaf comparison on the action map and on both product projections gives the same action square for the finite-product construction in the operations definition. By step 5 this becomes $\Lambda_U$-linearity after changing scalars along $c$. Concretely the balanced maps $m\otimes r\mapsto r\,\theta_M(m)$ induce a sheaf map $\rho_M:j^*M\to M\circ v$ using the sheaf tensor product. Its inverse is $n\mapsto\theta_M^{-1}(n)\otimes1$. The inverse composites are identities by $dc=\theta_{\Lambda_X}$ and the balancing relation $m\otimes r=c^{-1}(r)m\otimes1$; the pure-tensor equalities extend to sheaves by their defining universal property. These maps commute with restrictions and module morphisms by the formulas, giving the required $\rho_{M,W}$ and both naturalities.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; scalar transport along an isomorphism as in def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations

proof.text: Finally compute the specified unit. The presheaf Kan adjunction sends a map $\beta:F\to u^pG$ to the map whose composite with $\iota_{V,\phi}$ is $G(\phi)\beta_V$. In particular the unit $F(V)\to PF(u(V))$ is $\iota_{V,\mathrm{id}}$: composing it with any map out of $PF$ recovers exactly that map's adjoint, so this identifies the unit of the stated Hom bijection. Sheafification composes this with its canonical map. For modules the adjunction in the operations definition first uses this abelian adjunction and then tensor extension: the tensor transpose of a linear map $h$ is $m\mapsto h(m\otimes1)$. Therefore $\eta_{j,M}(V)$ sends $m$ to the sheafified coprojection $\iota_{V,\mathrm{id}}(m)\otimes1$. Put $W=u(V)$. The unique arrow $t_W\to(V,\mathrm{id})$ of step 1 has underlying map $a:W\to V$ equal to the projection. Steps 2, 3 and 6 now give $\rho_{M,W}(\eta_{j,M}(V)(m))=M(a)(m)$, exactly the asserted restriction. Step 4 shows the same formula after small-model transport. No quasi-compactness, support condition or constructibility was used.
